The present DAR (Detailed Accident Report) for compensation relates to simple injuries suffered by the claimant Sh. Hans Raj in a road accident that took place on 22.07.2014 at about 07:30 a.m.,
at Palam Flyover side, Delhi Cantt., New Delhi, regarding which an FIR bearing No.431/14, under Sections 279/337 IPC was registered at PS Delhi Cantt.

The offending vehicle involved in this case is a car bearing registration No. DL-8CU-2248, which at the time of accident was being driven by respondent no. 1 (R-1) Sh. Jitender Pal Singh, owned by respondent No.2 (R-2) Sh. Pankaj and Hansraj vs Jitender Pal on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68926729/
1 insured with respondent no. 3 (R-3) ICICI Lombard GIC.
2.

Succinctly put, facts of the case as per DAR are that on the aforesaid date, time and place of accident, the claimant Sh. Hans Raj was travelling in his vehicle i.e. car bearing registration No. DL- 9CZ-1447 to his workplace from his home.

At around 7:30 am when he reached near Palam flyover,
a car bearing registration no. DL-4C- AN-9273 which was moving ahead of him applied brakes.
Upon this, the claimant also applied brakes of his car.

At that point of time, the offending vehicle i.e.
Swift Dzire car bearing registration no. DL-8CU-2248 which was being driven by the driver/R-1 in a rash and negligent manner hit the claimant's car from behind.
The impact was so forceful that claimant's car hit the car ahead of him and claimant suffered injuries.
FIR No. 431/2014 u/s 279/337 IPC was registered against R-1.
The injured was treated at DDU Hospital.

As per the MLC,
the injured/claimant suffered simple injuries.
3. In his Written Statement, R-1 has denied the allegations of the claimant.
It has been submitted that the claimant did not receive any injury in the incident and it was the claimant himself who was driving his car negligently.
4. In his Written Statement, R-2 has denied the allegations of the claimant.
It has been submitted that the claimant did not receive any injury in the incident and it was the claimant himself who was driving his car negligently.
5. R-3/Insurance Company did not take any statutory defence.
It placed on record the legal offer in sum of Rs. 7,000/- along with expenses on treatment.
6. The legal offer of the Insurance Company was not accepted by the claimant.

Accordingly,
following issues were framed on 17.11.2015:
1.

Whether the claimant sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 22.07.2014, at about 7:30 AM at Palam Flyover side, Delhi Cantt., New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-8CU-2248 driven by respondent no.
1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.
2.
Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP.

He has proved photocopy of his Aadhaar Card as Ex.PW1/1 (OSR).

His medical treatment record is Ex.PW1/2 (colly).
8.

The Tribunal heard the arguments advanced by Sh. Dinesh Kumar, Ld. Counsel for the claimant,
Ms. Manu Kushwaha, Ld. Counsel for R-3/Insurance Company and Sh. Neeraj Bhushan, Ld.
Counsel for R-1 and R-2.
The case record has also been carefully perused.
The finding on the aforesaid issues is reproduced in succeeding paragraphs hereinafter.
ISSUE No.1 1.

Whether the claimant sustained injuries in the accident which occurred on 22.07.2014, at about 7:30 AM at Palam Flyover side, Delhi Cantt., New Delhi caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. DL-8CU-2248 driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 ? OPP.
10.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant.
In order to prove negligence of respondent No. 1, the claimant has examined himself as PW-1.
In his cross-examination, he has deposed that he was driving a Nano car at the time of accident.
He also denied the suggestion that due to traffic jam and the vehicle ahead of him, he had to applied brakes suddenly because of which accident took place.
He clarified that there was no traffic jam at the time of accident.
11. The chargesheet annexed with the DAR corroborates the evidence of PW1 to the effect that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by R- 12.

Reliance is also being placed upon the judgments in cases National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs.
Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287 and United India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Deepak Goel and Ors. , 2014 (2) TAC 846 (Del.) decided by the Coordinate Bench of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court, wherein it was held as under :-
"......where the claimants filed either the certified copies of the criminal record or the criminal record showing the completion of investigation by police or issuance of charge sheet under Section 279/304A IPC or the certified copy of FIR or the recovery of the mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle, then these documents are sufficient proof to reach to a conclusion that the driver was negligent particularly when there is no defence available from the side of driver."

15. Pertinently, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to rebut his involvement in the aforesaid accident, which he has failed to do.
He has not led any evidence to show that he was not driving his vehicle rashly and negligently and under what circumstances had the accident taken place.

Therefore, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

sentences.text: It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an Accident Tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.

Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in case titled as Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
17.

sentences.text: In view of foregoing discussion, it is held that oral evidence led on record by PW1 on this issue is duly substantiated by the documentary evidence i.e. chargesheet, and thus, it stands proved on preponderance of probabilities that the aforesaid accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle bearing No. DL-8CU-2248 which was being driven by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent No. 2 and insured with respondent no.3.
Hence, this issue is decided in favour of the claimant and against the respondents.
2. Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
18.

As the issue No.1 has been proved in favour of the claimant, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
19. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)
(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.

20.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 21.
Even though, in the MLC, the injured/claimant suffered simple injury, the medical documents (Ex.PW1/2) show that he suffered injury in cervical spine and also suffered swelling in the upper limb.
Cervical collar was applied for stabilization of neck.
Medical documents dated 30.07.2014 further show that the cervical collar was prescribed for one month.
His medication continued and on 12.08.2014, further medication and cervical collar was prescribed for a month.
Medical documents dated 14.08.2014 show that he suffered mild distal demyelinating sensory motor polyneuropathy.
In other words, he suffered mildly decreased ability to move and feel in both upper limbs.
From the record, it appears that hospitalization for five (05) days was advised by Rockland Hospital.

There is,
however, nothing to show that the claimant had actually got himself admitted.
22. The claimant has tendered on record his original medical bills as Ex. PW1/2 (colly) which are totalling to a sum of Rs. 22,772/-.
During cross examination, he admitted that he has not received any reimbursement of his medical expenses from his Department.
Further, the respondents have failed to lead any evidence to show that the said medical bills do not relate to the injuries suffered by the claimant in the aforesaid accident.
Thus, the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses remained unrebutted and uncontroverted.
In the absence of any plausible evidence produced by respondents on record, there is no reason to disbelieve the testimony of PW-1 that he had spent the aforesaid amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, he is held entitled to Rs.22,772/- towards his medical expenses.
(ii) Loss of earning 23.
The claimant in his affidavit has claimed that he was working as government servant with Delhi Police.
During cross examination, he deposed that he was working as Head Constable with Delhi Hansraj vs Jitender Pal on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68926729/

sentences.text: 5 Police at the time of accident and was earning about Rs.40,000/- to Rs.50,000/- per month and presently, he is earning Rs. 70,000/- per month.
During examination, he admitted that he has not filed any salary slip and leave record.
He further deposed that he took about one week off from his department for his accidental injuries and thereafter, he resumed his work and was assigned light duty.
24. Perusal of record reveals that the claimant was advised one month bed rest by Joint and Spine Clinic on 30.07.2014 and on 28.08.2014, doctor opined that the injured was fit for light duty.

25. Since the salary and employment of the claimant has not been established on record, the minimum wages of unskilled person is taken into account as per rates prevalent in Delhi, which was Rs. 8,554/- per month at the time of accident.
26. Keeping in view the medical history and continued medical treatment, this tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of one month.

Therefore, under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs. 8,554/- (Rs. 8,554/- X 1 month).
(iii) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities.

27. As stated above, the claimant had suffered simple injuries in the accident, but the medical documents show that he had suffered injury in cervical spine and also suffered swelling in the upper limb and cervical collar was applied for stabilization of neck.

Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which the injured had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- each is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings and Rs. 20,000/- towards mental and physical shock.
However, the claimant is not held entitled to any loss of amenities.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.70,000/- under this head.
(iv) Conveyance, Special Diet and Attendant Charges 28.
The claimant is silent with regard to the amounts spent towards special diet, conveyance and attendant charges.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.5,000/- each is being awarded to the claimant towards conveyance and special diet.
Considering the nature of injuries, no attendant charges are however, awarded.
Thus, the claimant is held entitled to an amount of Rs. 10,000/- under this head.
ISSUE No. 3/Relief 29.

In view of foregoing discussion, the claimant is thus awarded a sum of Rs.1,11,326/- (Rupees One Lakh Eleven Thousand Three Hundred Twenty Six only) (Rs. 22,772/- + Rs.8,554/- +

However, it is directed that the amount of interim award and interest for the suspended period, if any, during the course of this inquiry, shall be liable to be excluded from the award amount.
RELEASE 30.
The entire awarded amount is directed to be released in the saving bank account of claimant through RTGS/NEFT or any other electronic mode.
LIABILITY 31.

All the respondents are though being held jointly and severally liable to pay the awarded amount of compensation to claimant, but respondent no.3 being insurer of offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the award amount with UCO Bank, Patiala House Court Branch, along with interest @ 7.5%
per annum from the date of filing of claim petition by RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in bank account being maintained in the above said bank in name of this tribunal within 30 days from today, failing which it is liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the period of delay.

In case even after lapse of 90 days from today, respondent no. 3 fails to deposit this compensation with interest, in that event, in light of judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Kashmiri Lal 2007 ACJ 688, this compensation shall be recovered by attaching the bank account of respondent no. 3 with a cost of Rs.5,000/-.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co.
Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 has observed that filing of charge sheet against the driver prima facie points towards his complicity in driving the vehicle rashly and negligently.
It has been further Hansraj vs Jitender Pal on 7 June, 2024
He has not led any evidence to show that he was not driving his vehicle rashly and negligently and under what circumstances had the accident taken place.
Therefore, an adverse inference is liable to be drawn against the respondent no. 1/driver in terms of judgment of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
16.
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an Accident Tribunal is similar to that followed by a Civil Court and in civil matters, the facts are required to be established on preponderance of probabilities and not beyond reasonable doubt, as are required in a criminal prosecution.
Reference in this regard is made to the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court reported as (2009) 13 SC 530 in case titled as Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, wherein it has been observed that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular vehicle in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants and the claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
17.
19. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
Though, it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which the injured had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.50,000/- each is being awarded to him towards pain and sufferings and Rs. 20,000/- towards mental and physical shock.
However, the claimant is not held entitled to any loss of amenities.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.70,000/- under this head.
